none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references: - Alexander Tyurin. [Near-Optimal Convergence of Accelerated Gradient Methods under Generalized and $(L_0,L_1)$–Smoothness](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.06884v2). 2025 preprint; 2026 publication (v2 used). Complexity: $O(1+\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+L_1\bar R\log_+\min\{L_1^2\bar R^2\Gamma_0/L_0,\Gamma_0R^2/\varepsilon\}+\log_+(\Gamma_0/L_0))$ exact gradient calls for AGD with increasing step sizes and $f(y)-f^*\le\varepsilon$; $R=\|x_0-x^*\|_2$, $\bar R\ge R$, $\Gamma_0\ge2\Delta/R^2$, and $\log_+t=\max\{0,\log t\}$.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable convex minimization on E, with an attained minimum; no strong convexity of f is assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Queries return the exact derivative in the dual space, for every history and seed.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Exact minimizer of v(u)+Bψ(u,z) over E. Gradient and prox queries share the single counted oracle budget; function values are unavailable.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Continuous derivative g satisfies ‖g(x)−g(y)‖≤(L0+L1 M)‖x−y‖ whenever its norm is bounded by M throughout the segment. Public parameters satisfy L0>0 and L1≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: Arbitrary norm and differentiable mirror function with Bψ(y,x)≥‖y−x‖²/2. A minimizer satisfies Bψ(x*,x0)≤D and f(x0)−f(x*)≤Δ, with public D,Δ>0; the mirror function is hidden behind the prox oracle.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real normed vector space.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying f(output)−f(x*)≤ε for a minimizer x*, with ε>0. ε is excluded from publicInput, so the algorithm is independent of the requested tolerance.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap bound holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Gradient-dependent segment smoothness combined with general Bregman geometry and a joint exact gradient/prox budget is a meaningful variant of standard smooth convex optimization.
